title: The Cause, Not The Copies
eyebrow: Done. All three gates are running, and the habit now costs a refusal instead of a repeat.

actions.fyi: Nothing is waiting on you. Every call is listed below and any of them can be sent back.

content.label: What goes wrong
content.lead: You point at a habit, I tidy the examples you pointed at, and the habit keeps producing more.

rows: The work items are written in words nobody outside the code uses
Rewrote the ones you had in front of you
Nothing checks the wording of a new one, so the next reads the same way

blocks.label: The shape of it
blocks.text: A complaint arrives naming examples, and the examples become the whole job.

content.label: Why it keeps happening
content.lead: Three reasons, and only the first is about me being lazy.

rows.title: Work about the product runs through a set of steps that already forces a root fix
rows.note: It has to be reproduced first, and it ends with something that goes red if the fault returns. A complaint about how I work never enters those steps at all — it is answered inside the same reply.

rows.title: Nothing asks what produced the examples
rows.note: The complaint is filed as the symptom you saw, and every step after that aims at the symptom.

rows.title: The step that stops a repeat can be dropped by writing one sentence
rows.note: Writing a sentence is always cheaper than building the check, so under any pressure the sentence wins.

content.label: What actually refuses
content.lead: Three gates. Each sits at a moment I cannot get around, and says no — none of them relies on me remembering anything.

rows: I try to finish a reply
The reply cannot end if you pointed at a habit and nothing on the board names what produced it. A reader looks at the exchange and decides; it does not need me to admit anything
I come back with the fault written down and reproduced, instead of a tidy-up
A piece of work tries to close

Closing is refused while nothing exists that goes red if the fault returns. Skipping that needs your words on the work, held to the same test already used for your approvals — my own reasoning is not accepted
Either the check got built, or you said out loud it was not worth building
A piece of work is made
A title you would have to decode is refused outright. Nothing is restricted to a set of approved words — the title is ordinary English, and three separate tests look for reasons to reject it
Titles you can read without asking me what one means

blocks.label: Both of mine were watched refusing, not just watched passing
blocks.text: Each refusal was deliberately switched off and the board's own test run went red, naming the thing that got through; switched back on, it went green again. Checked by someone who wrote neither of them. A gate that has only ever been seen passing proves nothing, which is why this was done at all. And what each one is measured against is not invented: it is the seven-and-zero above — my reasoning refused, your words let through — so the check and the fault it catches are the same shape.

blocks.label: Why this section exists
blocks.text: The first version of this page listed the same three fixes as intentions with nobody enforcing them — the exact fault it was diagnosing. You caught it.

content.label: How big it actually is
content.lead: Measured before anything was built, by running the plain-words test your report pages already use over every open ticket title.

tiles.key: skipped the catch and said why

blocks.label: Every skip so far was mine to give
blocks.text: Seven jobs skipped building the thing that catches the fault coming back. Every one of the seven was waived on my own reasoning, and not one carried a word from you. A further twenty-eight skipped it before the board asked for a reason at all — those are counted separately rather than passed off as zero.

blocks.label: That one is closed now, and it bites today
blocks.text: The refusal is built and running. Four jobs already in flight will hit it the moment they take their next step, and they will have to either build the check or come to you for the waiver. It stops them at their first step rather than their last, so nothing gets built to a shape with no check in it and then has a check bolted on to fit.

blocks.label: The board fails its own test
blocks.text: One of the words it refuses is a word the board writes into titles by itself, on every job, without anyone typing it. So this is not two tickets you happened to see — it is a third of the board, and some of it the board wrote.

blocks.label: The title gate landed — from the other session, not this one
blocks.text: The word half is live: a title written in our own words is now turned away at the moment work is made, and told which plain word to use instead. That is the third of the board above, closed at its source, by the session that was already on it. The reading that catches our private meanings sits on top of it and is now unblocked.

content.label: What the outside reading found
content.lead: Someone who never saw the work being done read all of it and checked twelve claims line by line. It confirmed the gates fire where they say they do — and found three things wrong. All three are fixed and on the main line.

rows.title: The off switch I told you about breaks the board's own test run
rows.note: I said there was a way to turn the reply gate off. There was, and using it made every check on the board go red — so it was not a way out, it was a second problem. Fixed: the switch works, and the board now checks itself twice more, once under each way of throwing it.

rows.title: A refusal that exists but has never fired reads exactly like one that was never built
rows.note: The numbers you are shown could not tell 'nothing has gone wrong yet' from 'nothing is watching', and those mean opposite things. Fixed: three answers now, and the report works out which by looking for the line that does the counting — so a refusal quietly deleted goes back to reading as missing, by itself.

rows.title: The refusal's own wording claims to be stricter than it is
rows.note: It told the agent its own reasoning would never be accepted, when in truth a single well-chosen word gets through. Reworded to promise only what it delivers and to name what it cannot catch — and it came out ten characters shorter, not longer.

blocks.label: And chasing the first one turned up something far worse
blocks.text: Fixing the off switch meant running the board's checks from a clean slate for the first time, and that exposed a fault nobody was looking for: under those conditions the checks were writing a wrong value into a file the real refusals read — which would have quietly disarmed every gate on the board, with everything still reporting green. Found and fixed. It is the reason the reading was worth paying for.

blocks.label: And the reader itself had a fault
blocks.text: It named those three in its own summary and then filed none of them, so they would have lived in a sentence nobody had to act on. I put them on the board by hand and wrote that failure down as its own fault.

content.label: What it costs you
content.lead: Almost nothing to run. The real cost is one extra step on faults, and it is the step that stops the fault coming back.

rows: Titles
Two tests are ordinary programs and cost nothing at all. The third asks a model about fifteen words
A rejected title means I write it again. Seconds, and it stops happening as I learn the standard
Closing
An ordinary program. Nothing
This is where the real cost sits: a fault now ships with something that catches it, which can double a small fix. Only faults, never features, and you can waive it
Ending a reply
A free word check runs first and settles most replies on its own. Only when it sees a sign of a repeat does a model read the exchange, so this fires a handful of times a session, not every turn
None, unless it catches something — and catching something is the point

tiles.key: of your messages get a reading
judged right on a test batch

blocks.label: And it is already running on you
blocks.text: One of your messages this session was screened, read, judged not a habit, and let straight through. That is the gate working in production rather than in a test: about 450 words of thinking spent, no wrong block, nothing for you to notice.

blocks.label: The estimate is now a measurement
blocks.text: Counted over every message this machine has kept: 1,441 of 19,257 got past the free check and were read. The rest cost nothing at all. That is the answer to what you asked, and it is smaller than the guess I gave you.

blocks.label: One thing you should know about it
blocks.text: The reading spends from your own allowance, and when that runs out it stops working — quietly, and exactly when sessions are busiest. It fails in the safe direction, which means it lets things through rather than blocking them, so a busy day is a day the gate is not really there. That has its own ticket. It cost us the outside reading of this very job twice before the allowance reset.

content.label: Who does the checking
content.lead: Two of the three are plain programs with no judgement in them. Only the first needs something that can read English, and even there the refusal itself is a program.

rows: Titles
A small program for the first two tests, and a short reading for the third — see the section below
The title itself, nothing else
No. There is no other way to make a piece of work; making one by hand is already refused
Closing
A small program. Built and running — it now stops a bug job at its very first step, before anything is designed or built
The record of that work: whether a check exists, and whether the waiver quotes you

Partly, and now measured. Every honest-sounding excuse I threw at it was turned away, but the single word approved gets through, so a determined forgery still would. That has its own ticket; the real fix is a signal I cannot write at all
Ending a reply

Three halves, cheapest first. A free word check on your message settles most replies alone. Only if it sees a sign of a repeat does a short reading — a model, not me, and not a full helper — decide whether you really pointed at a habit. Then a plain program refuses the reply if that flag is up and nothing on the board names a cause
Your message, and the work created during that reply
No, because the flag is set before I write anything and the refusal never asks my opinion

blocks.label: I told you no fallback was needed. That was wrong
blocks.text: The route the documentation implied does not exist: a reading attached that way leaves no trace anyone can read afterwards, and making it say no erases your message instead of flagging it. Both were proved with live runs before anything was built on them. So the fallback is what shipped — and it is the cheap-first version you were already quoted: a free word check on every message, a reading paid for only when that check sees something. The part that mattered is intact — it still judges your message as it arrives, before I have written a word.

content.label: Your jargon complaint, worked through
content.lead: A title is ordinary English of any length. Three tests look at it, and any one of them can refuse it.

rows: Words we have already been caught using, each stored with the plain replacement
Terms from the trade, the moment one leaks back in
Anything invented after the list was written
The shapes code leaves behind — file names, run-together words, brackets, shouted initials
Terms nobody has seen before, recognised by how they look rather than what they mean
Invented words that look like ordinary English
A short reading, asking one question: would you have to ask me what this means
Our own private meanings — which is the thing you actually complained about
It is a judgement, so it will sometimes be wrong in both directions

blocks.label: Your question just moved the design
blocks.text: A list of banned words would have missed your complaint completely. The titles that annoyed you are not terms from the trade — they are ordinary words carrying a private meaning we invented, and no list catches those. Without your question the fix would have shipped catching the wrong thing.

rows: A reader is fired at the job and signs the job
Someone who did not do the work checks it, and their name goes on it
Every review item is retired and none can be made
Work waiting to be checked vanishes, and no new check can be started

decisions.title: Your words are the test for the title of a piece of work
decisions.why: You read those titles. The report pages already refuse our own vocabulary, so the standard is set.

decisions.title: Skipping the permanent fix stays possible, but it is your call and not mine
decisions.why: Some faults really are one-offs, and a guard for those costs more than the fault ever will.

decisions.title: This lives in the machinery, not in a written rule
decisions.why: A written rule is one I can read past. A refusal is not.

decisions.title: Nothing here changes the product
decisions.why: It only changes how a complaint from you is handled, so it cannot cost you a render or a frame.

decisions.title: Each gate ships with the fault it is supposed to catch, put in on purpose
decisions.why: A gate that passes proves nothing. It counts once we have watched it go red on a fault we planted.

decisions.title: The first gate is judged by a separate reader, not by me declaring myself clean
decisions.why: Noticing my own habit is exactly the thing I am bad at, so the judgement cannot be mine.

decisions.title: The free check always runs first, and the paid one only on suspicion
decisions.why: Asking a model on every reply would be the expensive way to build this, and almost every reply has nothing to find.

decisions.title: The counter that measures the cost is built before the gates it measures
decisions.why: Otherwise the first number we have to argue about is one nobody can check.

decisions.title: All three gates get built, at their strongest setting
decisions.why: Your answer on 2026-08-14 was "do it", against a page recommending all three, the hard version of each.

decisions.title: A habit you point at is always written down as work, never answered on the spot
decisions.why: Your first answer. It costs a slower reply the first time and it is the only way the cause gets looked at.

decisions.title: Finishing is refused until something catches the fault coming back, and only your words waive it
decisions.why: Your second answer. Mine were the reasons that let the check get skipped every time.

decisions.title: The title reading waits for the other session's half instead of racing it
decisions.why: Two of us building the same refusal on the same entry point is the waste this whole job exists to stop.

decisions.title: The reading judges your message as it arrives, not the reply afterwards
decisions.why: It then never sees my account of what you meant, which was the weak point of judging at the end.

next.if_nothing: Nothing. The three gates are running and you will only notice them when one of them stops me.

steps.step: The reading that catches our private meanings goes on top of the word check, now that the word check has landed
A signal you cannot be impersonated with, so a waiver is provably yours rather than merely worded like you
Say out loud when the reading has gone quiet on a busy day, instead of letting the gate lapse in silence
